rationale.conceptual: The method uses standard DFT GSF calculations and solution energy formulas. It requires careful supercell construction (including hydrogen SQS for δ-phase) and extraction of SSF/USF from displacement curves, but the approaches are well-established in the field; no novel algorithms or derivations are needed.
rationale.execution: The pipeline demands orchestrating many DFT runs across multiple coverages and displacement grids, setting up slab geometries, performing constrained relaxations, and post-processing energy curves to extract SSF/USF values. This involves non-trivial tooling and many steps, though the overall number of stages is manageable.

difficulty.reasoning: The task involves reproducing DFT stacking fault energies and solution enthalpies for Zr-Sn systems using standard computational methods. The conceptual complexity is moderate: it requires setting up slab supercells, performing generalized stacking fault calculations with rigid shifts, and computing solution enthalpies, all of which are established in the literature. The execution is demanding because it orchestrates many individual DFT runs across multiple coverages and displacements, requires careful post-processing to extract SSF and USF values, and relies on non-trivial DFT tooling and convergence management.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT supercell calculations with ~100 atoms and 500 eV cutoff do not require GPU; memory per simulation is moderate (up to ~32 GB to allow parallel runs). Only input crystal structures are needed, no large datasets.
